subject: Agriculture
title: Fertigation
description: A micro-lesson that makes Fertigation usable.

hook.text: Why water fields and then spread fertilizer separately? Fertigation does both at once.

buildup.text: Dissolved nutrients are injected into irrigation water and delivered directly to plant roots through drip lines.

discovery.text: Plants absorb nutrients more efficiently in dissolved form. Less fertilizer is needed for the same yield.

twist.text: Over-fertigation contaminates groundwater. Precise dosing requires sensors and careful management.

climax.text: Modern fertigation systems adjust nutrient mixes automatically based on soil sensors and growth stage.

punchline.text: Feed the plant, not the field. Precision pays.

quiz.question: What is fertigation?
options: Injecting dissolved nutrients into irrigation water delivered to roots

details.summary: Fertigation combines fertilization and irrigation by dissolving nutrients in irrigation water and delivering them directly to root zones. This topic covers the technique's efficiency, compatibility with drip systems, and how it reduces both fertilizer waste and environmental pollution.
details.whyItMatters: Fertigation increases nutrient uptake efficiency to 80–90%, compared to 40–60% for conventional soil-applied fertilizer. It saves money and dramatically reduces nutrient runoff into waterways.
takeaways: Fertigation delivers nutrients with irrigation water directly to the root zone
Nutrient use efficiency can reach 80–90% versus 40–60% for broadcast application
Fertigation works best with drip irrigation for the most precise nutrient delivery

faq.question: What is fertigation and how does it work?
faq.answer: Fertigation injects dissolved fertilizers into an irrigation system—typically drip lines—so that water and nutrients reach plant roots simultaneously. Injection pumps or venturi devices control the concentration and timing of nutrient delivery.

faq.question: What are the advantages of fertigation over traditional fertilization?
faq.answer: Fertigation improves nutrient uptake by delivering nutrients directly to roots in dissolved form, reduces fertilizer use by 20–50%, minimizes runoff and leaching, can be adjusted in real time to crop growth stage, and saves labor from separate applications.
